column3: Saori Route ・ Plan Execution Report
I stayed at home today, letting time pass while flipping my reference books open and closed.
...At that point, Saori called me and asked me out.
Sorry, did I make you wait?
No, I just arrived too.
It's been a while since I last met her...
But she looks extremely worn out...
I see. Then it's alright.
At this point, some people walked past us and said...
No matter how good the terms are, 【if the compatibility is bad, it's impossible】 for a relationship to continue.
Them normalfags. Anyway, there's no one I can go out with lol.
...We could hear such stuff being said.
To Saori who went for an unreasonable marriage interview, and pushed to an engagement, this was the last thing she wanted to hear.
Saori seemed to have heard the conversation earlier, and had a depressed look on her face.
Kyo-Kyousuke-shi!
If we keep waiting here, we'll be bothering the maids who are distributing tissues.
Therefore, how about spending the rest of our time at the usual maid cafe?
So... how was it?
...No good.
Argh...
I'll repeat his words as he said them...
I understand what you're saying. Being otaku is not evil.
However, it's not a virtue either.
I don't hate otakus. I understand that there are some good points about anime and games.
However, it's a fact that a lot of people have become too deeply immersed and lost themselves in anime and games.
I don't want you to lose your original self.
...this is what he said.
Hmm, it's a very proper opinion.
Yes. Very proper.
However, my original self does comes from otaku hobbies.
That's why, having otaku hobbies rejected feels like having myself rejected too...
So you don't know how to deal with your fiance?
It's embarrassing, but it is as you said.
Oh right, there's something from Kuroneko.
This looks like it's going to take some time, so maybe I should hand this over first?
But, if I hand it over now, it would break the flow of conversation...
And this thing, it's excessively ominous.
And from what Kuroneko said, it doesn't give that good of an impression.
The design feels kind of cursed; guess it can wait.
Is something the matter, Kyousuke-shi?
...Nah, it's nothing.
Anyway, I'll return it to Kuroneko. Yeah, that's fine.
I stuffed the bracelet I pulled out in the back of my back pocket, and resumed the conversation.
Actually, there's something that Kuroneko asked me to pass to you, but...
Could you accept it?
Although it's a bracelet of really bad taste...
Why does Kuroneko-shi want to give this to me?
Sorry... I told Kuroneko about your hospitalization.
...Is that so.
Uhh, Saori's resentful gaze pierced my heart...
But...
I'm thankful for Kuroneko-shi's concern.
Saori couldn't help but shrug her shoulders, and took the crystal skull bracelet from me.
Fu fu... this is...
This design is like the incarnation of Kuroneko's hobby.
Same thoughts here.
However, I've heard that amulets which are purposely modeled to be ominous can still ward off evil.
Is that so?
But whether it applies to this thing, I'm not able to tell.
Laughing cheerfully, Saori put the bracelet on her arm.
You have my thanks as well.
Yeah, no biggie.
Besides that, let's get on the main point.
Sir yes sir!
Well then, Kyousuke-shi.
Let us meet again!
Y-Yeah.
Looking at Saori's back as she left, I had an unexplainable feeling of unease...
At this instant, somehow I got a feeling that Saori's wish would never come true.
Could this be a mysterious premonition?
I don't have a sixth sense though...
Anyway, I shouldn't give Saori that bracelet.
S-sorry, Saori! Could you return that bracelet to me, after all?
Eh? Why?
Actually, it seems that this bracelet was supposed to be for me.
For you?
Yup. If you put this on, a lot of bad things will occur.
According to Kuroneko, although this bracelet didn't fit her wavelength, it does have an effect.
She said that Saori might be able to do something with it, so she passed it to you.
Hmm...
Basically this bracelet has a troublesome history?
That's right.
It might or might not have an effect just like what Kuroneko says...
But if it had a negative effect, I would feel bad.
I see. As you said, it makes sense.
However, I can't bring myself to put Kuroneko-shi's good intentions to waste...
Then, I'll keep it along with your otaku goods.
After you've solved your problem, you can take it back.
If the owner can banish bad luck, then this cursed bracelet won't be able to exert its effect.
Well, that's true.
So let's do as you say, you can keep the bracelet for me.
Okay!
I took the bracelet from Saori, and put it into my back pocket.
After that, Saori clasped her hands together, and slightly lowered her head.
May Kyousuke-shi be protected by God...
...Please don't joke about it.
However, I learned something from this.
There's an unfillable gap between him and I.
Saori...
He's a good person. But...
Otaku hobbies are my... self-identity.
That's why, to not accept that...
I can't consider the marriage with him.
As Saori continued talking, she looked so worn out that it hurt my heart.
The big, tall, otaku-fashioned, swirly glasses Saori.
However, she's a normal high-school girl on the inside. Just a fragile girl.
About the marriage, leaving the past aside, it's considered too early for Japan in the current times.
It might still be true for the "refined world" that Saori lives in, but I've been ignoring that.
...But that's wrong. Saori's lost over it. She's troubled about it.
It's a marriage, isn't it? Jumping past the boyfriend-girlfriend relationship, into lifelong partners?
It's not a problem a 16-17 year old girl can solve on her own!
